t: San Francisco enacts 45-day citywide data center moratorium
b: Mayor Daniel Lurie signed a moratorium the Board of Supervisors had approved unanimously the week before. It pauses data center development while the Planning Department studies impacts and drafts controls.
iw: Short citywide pause in a market with little data center development.

t: Imperial County reinstates data center moratorium after court blocked the first
b: Supervisors unanimously adopted a new temporary freeze on data center projects on county land, citing water supply, pending applications and the environmental-review ruling. It responds to a judge's order to stop enforcing the June moratorium. An advisory committee is due to report in January.
iw: New county-wide freeze halts pending data center applications.

t: Oakland council unanimously approves 45-day data center moratorium
b: The council paused approvals of land-use agreements and entitlements for data centers while staff study energy, water, health and environmental effects. The pause can be extended. It followed a proposal to convert part of a downtown building into a data center.
iw: Short pause on approvals; extension possible but project is small.

t: Mendocino County extends data center moratorium to August 2028
b: Supervisors voted 4-1 to extend the pause by about 22 months, the longest state law allows. Facilities under 3 megawatts are exempt, and the pause ends sooner if a permanent ordinance is adopted.
iw: Nearly two-year pause blocks projects over 3 megawatts.

t: Court voids Imperial County data center approval, orders environmental review
b: A judge ruled the county improperly skipped state environmental review when it approved a lot merger for a roughly 1-million-square-foot data center complex. Development is halted until a CEQA analysis is done. The developer plans to seek a new trial or appeal.
iw: Court halts the state's largest proposed project pending environmental review.

t: Mendocino County adopts 45-day urgency data center moratorium
b: Supervisors approved a 45-day urgency ordinance pausing data center development, set to expire October 16.
iw: Temporary pause in a county with little data center activity.

t: Eureka council unanimously pauses new data centers for 45 days
b: The council voted 5-0 for a 45-day moratorium while staff study limits based on water use, electrical load or size. It can be extended up to two years with a four-fifths vote. Members cited rates, water and battery fire risks.
iw: Temporary pause that may be extended while rules are drafted.

t: Coachella adopts permanent citywide data center ban
b: The council passed an ordinance prohibiting data centers in the city, citing strain on power, water and noise. It follows a June moratorium and cancellation of a developer agreement for a 240-acre campus. It is the first permanent ban in the Coachella Valley.
iw: Permanent ban forecloses new projects in the city.
